interest: This cross-reference sheet highlights the diplomatic friction and maneuvering between Vichy France and Imperial Japan in late autumn 1940 following Japan's initial military entry into northern French Indochina in September 1940. It reveals Japanese efforts to probe and project naval power into southern French Indochina under the pretext of a cruiser 'courtesy visit' to Saigon, alongside the Vichy French government's cautious diplomatic resistance and delaying tactics. Additionally, it provides a valuable archival trail connecting State Department records on Japanese internal and naval affairs (decimal file 894.3351G) to French-Indochinese political files (751g.94/252).
overview: This file consists of a single-page State Department cross-reference sheet dated November 22, 1940, indexing Telegram No. 1007 (sections 1–5) sent from France by H. Freeman Matthews and originally filed under 751g.94/252. The document records a Japanese diplomatic request for authorization for an Imperial Japanese Navy cruiser to pay a courtesy visit to Saigon in early December 1940. It notes the French response stipulating that any such request had to be addressed directly to the French Government and that, under prevailing political and military circumstances, the French Government would request the postponement of the proposed voyage.

subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram No. 1007 (Sections 1–5) sent from France on November 22, 1940, by Chargé d'Affaires H. Freeman Matthews, with the original document filed under 751g.94/252. The subject note outlines a Japanese request seeking permission for a cruiser to make an official courtesy call at the port of Saigon in early December 1940. In response, the French government stated that formal requests must proceed directly through the French Government and indicated that, given current conditions, it would ask that the visit be postponed.
